_comment: ACTION-FIRST CUA site lane. Every task must END IN AN ACTION COMPLETED or ARTIFACT PRODUCED (file/route/cart/post/config/edit), NOT content browsing. auth_required marks tasks whose completion needs an account/login/payment so the auth-capture lane can take them; auth_required=false tasks complete anonymously. Inline-authored installment (2026-06-13) while subagent fan-out was rate-limited; target is 300 sites. Tasks phrased as user intents, robust to cosmetic UI change, ending in a visually checkable accomplished state.

tasks.instruction: Open a new 800x600 document, draw a filled rectangle on it, then export the result as a PNG so the export/download dialog with the PNG is shown.
Create a new document, add a text layer reading 'SALE', change its font size, and export the image as JPG ending on the save dialog.
Upload one of the sample images, let the background be removed, and reach the download button for the cut-out result.
Draw two rectangles connected by an arrow, label one of them, then export the canvas as a PNG ending on the export dialog.

Edit the diagram code to add a new node and edge to the flowchart, see it render, then reach the SVG/PNG export action.
Enter the function y=x^2-4 into the expression list and add a second function y=2x+1 so both curves are plotted on the graph.
Open the palette generator, lock one color, regenerate the others a few times, and reach the export/save-palette action.
Paste a code snippet, change the color theme, and reach the export button to produce a downloadable code image.
Get driving directions from Boston, MA to New York, NY, then add a stop at New Haven, CT so the multi-stop route with total time and distance is shown.
Get public-transit directions between two named stations in a city, then change the departure time so an updated transit itinerary with departure times is shown.
Search round-trip flights between two cities for given dates, filter to nonstop only, sort by price, and select a specific flight so its detail/continue screen is shown.
Plan travel from Lisbon to Madrid, open the train option, and expand it so the detailed schedule and price for that leg are shown.
Start a new system build, add a CPU and a compatible motherboard from the part pickers, and reach the build summary showing both parts and a compatibility note.
Search train connections from Berlin to Munich for a chosen date and time, then open one result so its stop-by-stop itinerary is shown (stop before booking).
Enter a home price, down payment, rate and term into the mortgage calculator and reach the computed monthly payment with the amortization breakdown shown.
Enter a multi-part computational query (e.g. 'distance from Earth to Mars today in light minutes'), run it, and confirm the computed result pods are displayed.
Search flights for a route and dates, apply a stops filter and a max-price filter, then select a result so its booking-options screen is reached.
Type a block of text into the new-paste editor, set an expiration and syntax highlighting, create the paste, and confirm the resulting paste URL/page is shown.
Write a short markdown note in the editor, set a custom URL, publish it, and confirm the published page with its edit code is shown.
Create a new poll with a question and at least three options, enable one setting, create it, and confirm the live poll/voting page is shown.
Search for a specific public-domain title, open its book page, and reach the EPUB download so the download begins or the file link is shown.
Browse to a specific ebook, open its page, and download the compatible EPUB so the download action completes.
Search for 'mountain sunrise', open a photo, and trigger the free download so the image download begins.
Write a title and a couple of paragraphs in the editor, then publish so the public article URL is shown.
Create a new Rich Text pad without logging in, type a heading and a bulleted list, and confirm the formatted content is in the document.
Write markdown with a header and a code block in the editor, see the live preview, and reach the export-as (HTML/PDF/Markdown) action.
Create a new markdown note, add a title and a checklist, and confirm the rendered preview reflects the content.
Search for 'wireless headphones', filter to 4+ stars and a price range, open a product, add it to the cart, and proceed to the cart/checkout page.
Search for an item, filter to 'Buy It Now' and a condition, open a listing, select options, and add it to the cart so the cart page is shown.
Search for a desk, filter by color, open a product, choose a variant, and add it to the bag so the shopping-bag summary is shown.
Find and complete a benefits/eligibility checker wizard with sample answers so it reaches a result/summary screen.
Use the postage price calculator: enter origin and destination ZIPs and a package size/weight, and reach the calculated shipping options/prices.
Start a new individual ESTA application, accept the disclaimers, and advance through the first applicant-information screen.
Start an auto-insurance quote: enter a ZIP and advance through the first vehicle/driver information steps toward a quote.
Launch the Tax Withholding Estimator and complete its first steps with sample inputs to reach a computed estimate screen.
Open the retirement benefit estimator and complete its initial inputs to reach an estimated-benefits result screen.
Open Pixlr E, create a new 800x600 white canvas, draw a filled rectangle using the shape tool, apply the Gaussian blur filter from the Filter menu, then export the result as a JPEG file.
In BeFunky, open the Photo Editor with a sample image, apply the Artsy effect from the Effects panel, adjust the intensity slider to 70%, then click Save and download the image as a PNG.
In BeFunky, open the Graphic Designer with a blank canvas, add a text element that says 'Summer Sale 2026', change the font to a bold style, resize the text box, then download the graphic as a JPG.
In LunaPic, upload a sample image using the URL upload option with any public image URL, apply a black border effect from the Draw menu, then save the resulting image to your computer.
In LunaPic, open a sample image from URL, apply the Cartoon effect from the Art menu, adjust if sliders appear, then download the cartoonized image.
In tldraw, draw three rectangles connected by arrows to form a simple flowchart, add text labels 'Start', 'Process', 'End' to each shape, then export the drawing as a PNG file using the Export menu.
In tldraw, use the pen tool to draw a freehand arrow, add a sticky note with the text 'TODO: Review this', draw a circle around an area, then export the canvas as SVG.

In JSFiddle, write HTML for a button labeled 'Click Me', add CSS to make it turn green on hover with a 0.3s transition, add JavaScript to display an alert saying 'Hello!' when clicked, then click Run to produce the live preview and save the fiddle.

In JSFiddle, write HTML with a <canvas> element 600x400, write JavaScript that draws a blue filled rectangle and a red circle on the canvas, click Run to produce the rendered canvas output, then save the fiddle.

In Godbolt Compiler Explorer, write a C function that computes the nth Fibonacci number using recursion, select GCC 13.2 as the compiler with -O2 optimization, observe the generated assembly output, then click Share and copy the short link to produce a shareable URL artifact.

In Godbolt, write a Rust function that sums a slice of integers, add a second compiler pane with a different Rust version, enable the diff view to compare the two assembly outputs, then share the session via the Share button to produce a permalink.

In DBFiddle with SQLite, write a CREATE TABLE statement for a 'products' table with id, name, price columns, INSERT five rows of data, then write a SELECT query that filters products with price > 10 and orders by price descending, run it to produce results, then copy the share URL.

In DBFiddle, write SQL to create two tables 'orders' and 'customers', insert sample rows, then write an INNER JOIN query that returns customer names with their order totals, run it to produce the result set, and share the fiddle URL.

On TableConvert, paste a CSV with 4 columns and 5 data rows into the CSV input tab, click Convert, switch to the Markdown output tab to see the formatted table, then click the Download button to save the Markdown file.
On TableConvert, switch to the JSON input mode, paste a JSON array of 5 objects each with keys name, age, city, click Convert, view the HTML table output, then download the HTML file.

On CSVJSON, paste a CSV string with headers 'id,product,price' and 5 data rows into the input area, click Convert, verify the JSON array appears in the output panel, then click the Download button to save the resulting JSON file.

On Beautifier.io, paste a block of minified JavaScript (a single-line bundle with multiple functions), click Beautify, verify the formatted multi-line output appears, change the indent size to 4 spaces, re-beautify, then copy the output to clipboard producing the formatted artifact.

On Diffchecker, paste original Python function text in the left panel and a modified version with 3 changed lines in the right panel, click Find Difference, review the highlighted diff output, then click Export to PDF to produce and download the diff report.

On Base64Encode.org, type a multi-line JSON string into the input field, select UTF-8 encoding, click the Encode button to produce the Base64 output string, then click the Download button to save the encoded result as a text file.

On QR-Code-Generator.com, select the URL tab, enter 'https://example.com/product/42' as the target URL, change the QR code color to dark blue, add a logo from the provided options, then click Download to save the QR code image as PNG.

On Favicon.io, use the Text to Favicon generator, type the letter 'A' as the text, set the background color to #3B82F6, set the font color to white, choose a rounded square shape, then click Generate and download the favicon package ZIP.
On Favicon.io, switch to the Emoji tab, search for and select the rocket emoji, then click Download to produce and save the favicon ZIP file.

On UUIDGenerator.net, navigate to the Bulk UUID Generation page, set the quantity to 50 UUIDs, select Version 4, click Generate, then copy all generated UUIDs to the clipboard to produce the UUID list artifact.

On Placehold.co, construct a URL for a 800x400 image with a dark background (#1E293B) and white text (#F8FAFC) displaying the text 'Product Screenshot', then open that URL in the browser and save the displayed placeholder image using right-click > Save Image As.

On CSGradient.io, set the gradient type to radial, add a third color stop at 50% with color #F59E0B, drag the first stop to position 10%, drag the last stop to position 90%, set the angle to 135 degrees, then click Copy to copy the CSS code and produce the gradient artifact.

On cubic-bezier.com, drag the first control point to approximately (0.17, 0.67) and the second to (0.83, 0.67) to create a bounce-like easing curve, compare it against the 'ease-in-out' preset using the comparison button, then select and copy the CSS cubic-bezier() value from the output field to produce the artifact.

On Clippy, select the Pentagon shape preset, then drag individual vertices to reshape the polygon into a custom arrow shape, observe the live preview update, then copy the generated clip-path CSS property value from the code box to produce the CSS artifact.

On SVGViewer.dev, click the Edit tab, paste SVG markup for a simple icon (a circle with a path), change the fill color attribute from black to #EF4444 by editing the code, click Render to preview the updated SVG, then click the Download SVG button to produce the file.

In GeoGebra, switch to the Geometry view, use the polygon tool to draw a triangle by clicking three points, use the perpendicular bisector tool on each side to find the circumcenter, then export the construction as a PNG.

In StackEdit, clear the default document, write a Markdown document with an H1 heading 'Project Proposal', two H2 subsections each with two bullet points, and a code block containing a Python snippet, then use the Export menu to export the document as an HTML file and download it.

On Lipsum.com, set the generation unit to 'Paragraphs', change the count to 5, check the 'Start with Lorem ipsum' checkbox, click Generate Lorem Ipsum, then select all the generated text and copy it to produce the placeholder text artifact.

Type 'expiry test note for cua' into the paste box, set the 'Paste Expiration' dropdown to '10 Minutes', click Create New Paste, and verify the new paste URL is displayed on the result page.

Type '# CUA heading\nbody text' into the editor, change the Format dropdown to 'Markdown', enable 'Burn after reading', set expiry '1 hour', click Send, and verify the encrypted paste URL is displayed.

On the paste.rs landing page, click into the textarea, type 'paste.rs CUA web test 2026', then submit the form (press the submit control or Ctrl+Enter). Confirm the browser navigates to the returned short URL and the raw text is shown.

Switch to the 'Upload via URL' tab, paste a public image URL (https://i.imgur.com/ ... or any direct image) into the URL field, click Upload, and verify the result box shows a new files.catbox.moe link to the rehosted file.

Open a public/demo contact form template that allows direct submission (or the Jotform 'Contact Us' demo). Dismiss cookie banner. Fill Name 'CUA Test', Email 'cua-test@example.com', and a Message 'Automated CUA submission 2026', then click Submit. Confirm the 'Your submission has been received' thank-you page is shown.

Confirm the 'Thanks!' completion screen is displayed.

Create a poll with question 'Tabs or spaces?' and options 'Tabs','Spaces', click Create Poll, then on the live page cast a vote for 'Spaces' and confirm the results bar chart updates and the share link is shown.

On the blank write.as editor, type a title line 'CUA Test Post 2026' then body 'Published anonymously by the CUA agent.', and click the 'Publish' button. Confirm the post is published at a write.as/ URL shown in the address bar and a 'View Post / Share' link is available.

Dismiss cookie/consent banner. Click into the rich editor, type 'JustPaste.it CUA publish test 2026 — heading and body text.', then click the 'Publish' button. Confirm the page redirects to the published justpaste.it/ short URL and shows the rendered note plus a share link.

In the txt.fyi editor type 'txt.fyi CUA minimal publish test 2026', then click the 'Publish' button at the bottom. Confirm the post is published to a unique txt.fyi/ URL displayed on the resulting page.

Dismiss cookie banner. Search for a public-domain title (e.g. 'Pride and Prejudice'), open its book page, click the 'Download' button, choose the EPUB format, and confirm a file download begins (download started indicator / browser download bar shows the .epub).

Dismiss cookie banner. Open a public-domain book from the catalog, on its detail page click the EPUB 'Download' button (free), and confirm the .epub download starts (browser download indicator appears).

Dismiss cookie banner. Search the catalog for 'Aesop's Fables' (or any short title), open the audiobook page, and from the chapter listing click an MP3 download link for one chapter. Confirm the .mp3 file download begins.

Dismiss banner. Search for a public-domain title (e.g. 'Alice in Wonderland'), open an edition that is 'Read' / public domain, click the download/format option (e.g. 'PDF' or 'Send to' → epub from the read panel), and confirm a downloadable file link is produced or a download starts.

Open a complete public-domain work's main page (e.g. search 'The Time Machine'), use the sidebar 'Download as EPUB' / 'Download as PDF' export tool, wait for the rendering job to finish, and confirm the generated EPUB/PDF file downloads.
Dismiss cookie banner. Search for 'mountains', open a photo result, click the green 'Free Download' button, choose the default/Original size if prompted, and confirm the .jpg image download starts.
Search 'coffee', open a photo, open the Download dropdown, select the 'Medium' size option, click Download, and confirm the image file download begins at the chosen resolution.

Dismiss any banner. Search 'forest', open an openly-licensed image result, click the 'Download' button (choose a size if offered), and confirm the image file download starts from the source.
